utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Ms. Thompson, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Gentlemen on both sides, there hasn't been a coup d'etat. The President, unfortunately, has flu and is indisposed, and he has asked me would I take over for today and possibly the next few days. The rules permit the Chamber to continue to sit in the absence of any of the Judges. Do any of you have a problem with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ms. President, no, we don't for the Prosecution. We absolutely do not object. And do think in addition to the provision that the Rule makes, I would ask that there be a clear acceptance by both Defence teams as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I understand that the President will be able to read the transcript, and he also will see the videorecording. But I'd just like to know how you feel about the Court proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Madam President, we have no problems whatsoever, no objections, and we're very happy. And we hope a speedy recovery for Judge Liu. My colleague -- we're not happy that Judge Liu is gone. We don't like to see him sick. We hope him a speedy recovery, but otherwise, no, we have no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You're happy to proceed. Thank you very much. Mr. Seric and Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Of course, I have nothing against it. And we should all abide by the Rule 15 bis. And indeed, it is only a matter of three days. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I notice that also the ranks of the Prosecution team and of the Defence team are somewhat slimmer than they used to be during the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I just say one last thing about how I am to be addressed. Whatever, madam or miss, but not Mrs. Very good. Could we bring the witness in, please. Mr. Scott, will you explain to Witness AD when she comes in, if she notices, why there are only two Judges instead of three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness AD, you're already sworn from yesterday. Are your earphones comfortable? Are you hearing properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, first of all, good morning. I hope your evening was as pleasant as possible in the circumstances. I want to remind you, of course, of the protective measures. And as we discussed yesterday, it is quite important for you to recall, and also for me, not to use family names such as your husband's name and those sorts of things that would tend to identify you or your family. Also, I would like to explain to you that you have now seen that we only have two Judges with us today, that Judge Liu is unavailable due to illness. And I wanted to explain that to you. It has absolutely nothing to do, of course, with your testimony. He simply has become ill. But under the provisions and practices of the Tribunal, we are proceeding with two Judges instead of three. All right. Thank you. Witness AD, yesterday afternoon, just to bring us a bit up to where we left off, you mentioned two things which will lead into my next series of questions. One was the situation where your husband had expressed fear that something would happen to him in connection with Stela. In fact, he told you that he was afraid that Stela would kill him. You then went on to tell us that your older son avoided arrest on the 30th of June, 1993, because he was essentially hiding in the house of his girlfriend, again, not mentioning her name. And you said that, if I'm correct, and, of course the record will govern, that the girlfriend's house was near Stela's headquarters. Is everything I've said so far, is that accurate? You'll have to give a verbal yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, what I want to have -- ask you next is: Did you know Stela? When your husband made these references to you about this person Stela, did you know that person, or prior to that time, or ever meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you say that your older son's girlfriend's residence was near Stela's headquarters, how did you know where or what Stela's headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all knew that it was in that building in Kalemova Street, both Stela and his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like, please, for the usher's assistance to show you Exhibit P15.2, which, if it's available, I think safely can be put on the ELMO without any disclosure issue. You can see that now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you describe that location to us. I mean, as what -- what you see on this photograph, what does that depict to you, if it does, if you know that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location that is at the intersection of Kalemova Street. It was a building. I can say even that it was painted pink. And that's where they had their base. It was that ATG, the anti-terrorist group. On the facade of this building, there were large-size letters "ATG" written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And of this particular ATG, did you know who or was there another name, a common reference to the -- to this headquarters, this being the headquarters of a particular soldier or officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They called it "the ATG group," those who were there. And I'm not aware of the building having had any particular name. I only knew that Stela was in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, directing your attention -- and we can leave the photo there, I think, for a moment. I want to direct your attention to the 12th of July, 1993. After your husband had been arrested on approximately the 10th of -- excuse me, I'm sorry, the 30th of June, did you see your husband on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around 9.00, I was just passing by this building where Stela's base was. And in the middle of the intersection, a truck stopped, and there were prisoners in it. They took them out of the -- off the truck and started lining them up against the building that was Stela's. I did not expect to see my husband. I was looking at him as he was looking at me. And they were all surrounded by armed soldiers. I passed by. I did not dare turn around to look. And I went home. My older son was at home, and I told him everything that I had seen. He said to me, "Mom, Stela will kill father."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, just to be -- while we have the photograph still on the ELMO -- let me just double-check. Your testimony just now, when you saw this group of prisoners and your husband on the 12th of July, it was in connection with the building which is shown on Exhibit 15.2, the one that's on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you see or can you recall what your husband was wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. He had a dark blue T-shirt and blue jeans, and he had one eye - I don't know which eye was shot - and he had burgundy-coloured moccasins.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, later that day - and we're still on the 12th of July - did you have occasion to go back to this building, this location, again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I again went back to that building because I wanted to see my husband. I was -- went behind a tree and saw him on his knees washing a car. I did not dare call him, and he didn't see me. And I saw him -- that he was weak and frail. He probably had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me back up for one moment perhaps. Did you ever -- did anyone else ever accompany you to this location before you saw your husband washing -- I just wanted to be sure that I had -- washing a car? Had you gone back to Stela's headquarters with somebody else before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, the evening around 6.00, we went to Stela's headquarters, my son's girlfriend and I. And we were thinking of bringing some cigarettes and some change of clothes. There were some soldiers there, and she recognised one of them. His nickname was Cica. We asked him whether we could leave some things for him, and he said that we should come at 9.00 in the evening. We did not because we did not dare go out in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Apart from this or in addition to this soldier Cica, did you or your older son's girlfriend recognise any of the other soldiers or know the name of any of the other soldiers you saw there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not recognise anyone else. I was a little lost because it was very hard for me to be standing in front of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And you said that, if I heard you correctly, even though you were invited to come back later that day with perhaps some cigarettes or other items, ultimately, you decided for some reason not to do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you just clarify, please. You've mentioned seeing your husband washing a car or cars. Was that before you went back with your older son's girlfriend? Was it before that, or was it after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us approximately from your vantage point - and I think you testified you hid behind a tree - approximately how far from your husband were you when you saw him washing the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was approximately 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness, before continuing, I want to tell you that I certainly do not want to cause you any unnecessary pain in bringing back some of these events to you, and I'm sorry for that. But of course, we need to hear -- it's very important that the Judges hear your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P48. I'll ask that that not be placed on the ELMO for obvious reasons. It should be in the binders if anyone else in the courtroom wants to look at it, Binder 1, Exhibit P48.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, can you look at Exhibit P48 and, just for the record say who that is, or was. I'm sorry, if you need to collect yourself, please take a moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to pause for a moment, both for your benefit -- I know the Judges are looking for the exhibit. And Witness AD, can you tell us, when you saw your husband on the 12th of July, 1993 washing the car at Stela's headquarters, is that the last time you saw him alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, did anyone else tell you later that same day, or maybe tell you after that day, but that they had also seen your husband that same day? Again, don't mention any names. But if you recall anyone else telling you that they had also seen your husband on the 12th of July, can you tell that to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I say the name of the person who told me this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you don't think it will --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, out of an abundance of caution, if we can go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are we in open session now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: About a week after seeing your husband on the 12th of July, you brought your older son back to your home or he returned to your flat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, did your older son ever tell you about anyone coming to the house -- and I'll be clear, both to you and for the benefit of the courtroom. This is not something you heard but something your son told you, if you recall. Did your older son ever tell you about someone coming to the house around that time and giving you information about your husband?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam President, this is -- this has been now a series of leading questions since yesterday. I think that the time has come for me to make an objection here. I have been patient because this, indeed, is a victim that we have in front of us. But at this point, I need to object because this is a third leading question in sequence. And I would ask the Prosecutor to either rephrase his question or approach it from another angle. This is -- this has been the third consecutive question in which the Prosecutor has been giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I wouldn't go quite that far, but there has been a little bit of leading. So Mr. Scott, I know it's difficult, but try, because Mr. Seric has made quite a valid objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, if you can just tell us, do you recall anyone coming to your flat around this time and giving any information about your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A soldier came around 11.00. I don't know exactly the date. His name was Dinko. And he said that my husband was certainly killed, that we should not go looking for him anywhere, and that's all he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm afraid I now must clarify something, because we may have combined -- or jumped from one thing to the other. The time when this Dinko came, were you present with your older son, or who received this information from Dinko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my older son who first got this information from Dinko. I was not at home. When I came in, I saw a soldier leaning on a rifle. Of course it wasn't easy for me, and I was scared. My son was sitting. And I asked, "Who is this?" And he told me. And he said, "Ma'am, I came to tell you that your husband has been killed." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm only going to -- Madam President, I'm only going to ask very limited questions of this witness on the topic related to the exhumation for reasons, I think, will become obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, you were not involved or present, if I can approach it this way, at the exhumation or autopsy concerning a body that was later identified as your husband; is that correct? You were not involved -- or present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, you'll have to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't. My elder son was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did your son ever -- your older son ever tell you about what he had seen -- and again, forgive me. I don't want to cover anything terribly unpleasant -- but how the body -- how he had identified the body? Did he talk to you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me much about it because it was very hard for him. After some time, I asked him some questions, and all he told me was that he had recognised a part of the jeans and the T-shirt and the belt -- the buckle of the belt that he had round the jeans - I also still remember what that buckle looks like - and also a part, a fragment of the red moccasins, dark red moccasins, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Judges, at some point prior to that time and to the unfortunate events involving your husband in the middle of July 1993, had your husband previously had a bullet wound to his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Lower leg, I guess. Now, I'm not quite sure whether he hurt himself or whether somebody else injured him. I'm really not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell the Judges, please, was your husband a big man? Was he tall and strongly built? Or can you just describe him -- forgive me. Can you just describe your husband to the Judges, please, in a physical way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband was rather tall, rather big. He had black hair, but it was already pepper and salt. And he was close to 2 metres tall, but I'm not able to tell you exactly his height. He was a very big man, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam President, in deference to the witness, I'm just trying to see what actually needs to be covered and what's already been covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Scott, you might ask this witness if she knows what size shoe her husband wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, are you familiar, do you recall the approximate shoe size of your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: 46/47. That will be the size.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I want to take you ahead to the 9th of August, just to finish -- and we're finishing your testimony now. What happened to you on the 9th of August, 1993, you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 9th of August, 1993, it was very difficult to live there. We dared not go out. My sons and I were there together. And it was Thursday. I believe it was the 7th or thereabouts. A uniformed man turned up at our door around noon and asked me whose flat is it? Is it a communal flat. And I said it wasn't. And then he asked me if we wanted to leave that flat and go somewhere else. And I said no, we didn't. And he just made -- moved his head, sort of nodded his head, and went down the stairs saying nothing else. And we were staying in our flat for those two or three days more. And after 12.00, between -- I mean at midnight, between the 8th and the 9th of August, somebody knocked at the door. And I asked, Who is it? And somebody responded from behind the door. And I asked him what did he want, without opening the door. And he said, Madam, open it. We've had a report, and we need to ask you some questions, and we shall come back immediately. I was very distraught because I had my two sons there, but I had to open the door and there were three soldiers there. They told us to get ready and come with them immediately. One of them was Sasa Sanivovic and Memeti. And I do not remember who the third man was or what he looked like. As we were in our beds, we came out barefoot, barely dressed. They put us in a car and took us in the direction of the cathedral. I was terribly frightened. Then they turned towards Rondo. We took the Liska Street. They took us behind the infirmary and near a tall building which was across the street from the Health Centre. They made us get off the car, and Sasa asked me, "Do you know who your husband was"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I caution you there. You might be about to say something in connection with your husband, which do I want to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, could we go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Very good. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness AD, you've heard the exchange, I assume, between Judge Clark and I in the last moment. Let's go back for a moment in open session. After the comment about your husband, you began to tell the rest of your story in terms of what happened next. If you can just start again, you started telling us what happened. If you could just tell us that again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. We were there. He fired into the air. We started for the street and then ran towards the demarcation line on the Bulevar. We crossed that line and crossed over to the left bank of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us, Witness AD, did you ever live in the flat you were evicted from around the early part of August 1993? Were you ever able to return to live in that flat again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never returned there, and it has been eight years now. We went there two months ago. We were allowed to go to our flat, but there was a family living there, and they were -- they had to leave the flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Witness AD, I thank you for your testimony. I'm sorry if I've caused you to have to talk about some very difficult things. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Who's going to do the cross-examination now? Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I am lawyer Branko Seric, and I am here representing Vinko Martinovic. I'd like to shed some light on certain matters, if possible. Could you please get the ELMO down so that I don't have to play hide and seek with the witness. Madam, during the direct examination, you affirmed that you last saw your husband on the 12th of July, 1997; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you please make a pause after you hear my question, because we speak the same language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, sorry. Bad habit. I think it's an obvious error, I suppose, but so the record can be correct, it was just said "1997," instead of "1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's quite true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That day, you also told the Chamber, a neighbour said sometime having seen your husband at Stela's around 6.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that conversation with your neighbour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was no conversation really. He merely said that he had seen him by Stela's building around 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And did you tell that neighbour that you had seen your husband that morning already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That day, you said that you had seen a man whose name, or rather, nickname, I suppose, was Cica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what did he tell you exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped when we saw him, and he told us that he was in the building, that he could not come out, and that we should come at 9.00 in the evening to bring him cigarettes, a change of clothes, and whatever else he might need.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that your husband had been taken back to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that your husband told you that once he was -- how he was once riding a bicycle on his way home and that on his way, Vinko Martinovic had told him, "Where are you, thief?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When was it that you talked about it the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean me and my husband?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I? Well, he came home and told me what had happened. He was very upset and said that Stela had told him, "Where are you, thief?"

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you tell anyone about this prior to your yesterday's testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did it ever occur to you to go to Vinko Martinovic and ask him what had really happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, because I dared not come near that building. And I think that from these statements, you can see how difficult it was for us Muslims during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please help me show the witness P520 it's in binder 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Don't, please, read it aloud, because there is some information which we should not make public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or perhaps we should go -- we could into private session, Madam President? No, I cannot put it on the ELMO either. Perhaps it would be best if we went into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, I was looking for the binder. Did you ask for private session? Yes, could we go into private session, then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Pages – 8208-8212 – redacted – private session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We'll all meet again here at 5 past 11.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: For the benefit of the translators and the stenographers, I thought it would be fair if we would take a short break at ten past 12.00 for 15 minutes and then if we sat until ten past or quarter past 1.00, and hopefully retrieve any lost time. Does that suit everybody?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps you could bring the witness in, and meanwhile Judge Diarra and I will read this document. Very good, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask that the witness be again handed the documents 520 and D2/14. Meanwhile, in order to speed up my cross-examination, could you also prepare the P774 exhibit for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Madam, were you able to find this special report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: On page 2, under number 15 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: -- do you see what is written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Under "15," it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we in the private session? Can we please go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We'll go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Madam, soldiers came to your apartment on three occasions. I forgot when the last time. When was the last time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of August. And they were there before as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were they members of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the HVO, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, I believe only one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, concerning the documents that you have been shown this morning about the alleged escape of your husband, just to clarify for the record in light of the exchanges that have taken place, do you know anything -- do you have any information that would indicate that these statements are based on anything more than the report made by someone in Stela's unit to someone at the Heliodrom? Do you have any other information at all about what these reports even are based on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was not a question in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The suggestion that her husband had escaped and there were reports to support it were the basis of your cross-examination. But the form of your question, Mr. Scott, is somewhat leading. Perhaps you could break the question up into a series of shorter questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, if you recall the documents that have been put in front of you in the last few moments or actually sometime -- and I'm sorry about any confusion about that. But in terms of anything in connection with the alleged escape of your husband, first of all, had you seen any of those documents before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you aware of any of the information, if any, on which those documents are based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of any information that would have been the basis for what is asserted in these documents, that your husband had escaped? Are you personally aware of any information that would support that allegation or assertion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I have not said this before, but while he was already at the Heliodrom, a person came. His name was Novica. He worked at the Heliodrom as a cook and had been arrested previously by the Serbs even. He came to our house and gave us the information [redacted]-- [redacted]. Thirty of them had been taken to perform labour. He was the thirtieth who did not come back. And we were -- and the word was that he had been shot and killed by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, there was the one reference, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. obviously, that will have to be redacted. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Diarra, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Clark. The answers given by the witness were so clear that I have only a few questions to put to her. Witness AD, you told us how you had been expelled from your flat. Could you help me by telling me whether or not you had the opportunity and whether your two sons had the opportunity to get their things back. Were you given that possibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. We left barefoot. It was summertime. It was the month of August. We left without anything. We were not allowed to take any possessions. Even the medication that I had, the medicines that I had picked up, they made me throw away. So I had nothing with me when we crossed to the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness AD. I would like to congratulate you on your calm and your great serenity. You have been quite composed during your testimony and this in spite of the grave events that you have been through. Thank you very much. And all the best for the future.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I have a question to ask you. During the period that your husband was in detention at the Heliodrom and before your expulsion to the east side, did you ever receive any official notification about the whereabouts or the fate of your husband from the HVO authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received any official notification. The only information was from Dinko, who was in Stela's base, and from Novica, who was at the Heliodrom, that he was confirmed dead. But we did not receive anything official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I join with Judge Diarra in wishing you the best for the future.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could we take the witness out. And again, thank you for giving your evidence to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam President, Mr. Stringer will be handling the next witness. It will be a protected witness, and I'm sure he'll want to deal with that in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid I'm losing count of whether we're in private session or not. But if we're not in private session, we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This message is for the people sitting in the public gallery. We will now be going into closed session, which means you will not be able to see nor hear the proceedings. This will probably take place for the duration of the time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Will we now go back into closed session. I think you all realise that I was never very good at high tech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of January, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.11 p.m.,
